newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-ROME MAYOR HAILS "SUCCESS FOR ALL ITALY".
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ROME MAYOR HAILS "SUCCESS FOR ALL ITALY".

text.p: Rome mayor Francesco Rutelli said the naming of his city in a short-list of candidates to host the 2004 Olympics on Friday was something that the whole country could be proud of as well as the capital.

"It's a success for Italy," Rutelli said after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) named Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town, Rome and Stockholm as the final candidates from among 11 cities bidding to stage the Games. The final vote will be in September.
Schoolchildren in Rome had gathered from the early morning at a city sports centre to hear the decision although a technical glitch disrupted a live link-up with Lausanne.
A giant heart of balloons in Rome's red and yellow colours was laid out in the centre of a running track.
"We can be proud of the work we have done, work to give great satisfaction to all Italy," said Rutelli.
"Great cities, great nations, are out of the Olympic race and we are still here in a tough fight but with our heads high.
"I think the merit belongs to all Italy, to the city, to the sporting organisations and CONI (the Italian Olympic Committee) which all make a good team together.".
Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni, who also has responsibilities for sport, said the IOC decision rewarded "a strong and credible bid".
"We congratulate the other cities and other countries selected before the final decision on September 5," he said. "All are serious and attractive proposals.
Rome is seen as the favourite for the final vote even though it has staged the Games before.
The city held the Summer Olympics in 1960 and has facilities which are the envy of many other candidates. Italy also hosted the soccer World Cup in 1990.
